title: Recoil and explosions
target: Use momentum conservation for an isolated system.
criteria: Choose a system and check external impulse.

authoring.limitations: Reasoning evidence only. Multiple choice does not certify physical performance. Teacher reviews before assigning and rates mastery separately.

cpa.prompt: Two carts push apart on a nearly frictionless track. Which system supports momentum conservation during the push?
options: One cart while ignoring the other’s force.
Both carts, with negligible net external impulse.
Only the spring’s color.
Both carts only if both final speeds are equal.
cpa.guide: Internal forces redistribute momentum within the chosen two-cart system.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: An explosion occurs while a large external impulse acts on the fragments. Which account is valid?
options: Only the largest fragment has momentum.
All fragment momenta must individually be zero.
Final system momentum equals initial momentum plus external impulse.
Momentum must remain unchanged regardless of external impulse.
cpa.guide: System momentum changes according to external impulse.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.

cpa.prompt: Two carts initially at rest separate. One has final momentum −15 kg·m/s. With negligible external impulse, what is the other’s momentum?
options: 0 kg·m/s
+15 kg·m/s
+30 kg·m/s
−15 kg·m/s
cpa.guide: Initial total is zero; the final momenta must sum to zero.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: A 3 kg cart recoils at −2 m/s. Its 2 kg partner moves right. Both began at rest with negligible external impulse. What is the partner’s velocity?
options: +3 m/s
+2 m/s
+6 m/s
−3 m/s
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Apply the physical relationship to new data.

cpa.prompt: Two unequal-mass carts push apart. Their mutual forces act over the same interval. Compare their momentum changes.
options: Equal magnitude and opposite direction.
Both changes point the same way.
Equal velocity changes in all cases.
The heavier cart gets more impulse.
cpa.guide: Equal-opposite forces over equal durations give equal-opposite impulses.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

cpa.prompt: A lighter and a heavier cart begin at rest and push apart in isolation. Which cart has greater speed afterward?
options: Neither can move if total momentum stays zero.
Both must have equal speed.
The heavier cart, because its momentum must be greater.
The lighter cart, because equal momentum magnitudes divide by different masses.
cpa.guide: |v| = |p|/m; equal |p| implies greater speed for smaller mass.
cpa.freshness: New scenario and/or model data, independently answerable without worksheet answers.

demand.evidence: Compare evidence and identify a physical relationship.
